subsystems.limits: Signed INT8 matrix and candidate INT32 vector operations use the pooled VGPR authority. Floating matrix formats, a full per-wave instruction-issue controller, synthesis, and physical evidence remain open.

Complete workgroups reserve actual pooled VGPR and local-memory resources and preserve barrier membership. A CU-local decoded workgroup dispatcher and C++ command-queue reference now feed the authoritative frontend; RTL/global queue processing, public ABI freeze, and runtime toolchain integration remain open.

Decoded per-wave requests, local-region access, global ready/valid boundary, writeback, faults, cancellation, barriers, quiescent release, and CU-local workgroup dispatch are integrated. A bounded C++ command-queue reference feeds the dispatcher; RTL/global queue processing, ISA memory decode, multi-CU placement, caches, MMU, fabric, and physical memory remain open.

cgx1_tile_power_manager drives cgx1_top.tile_enable from board-state caps, actual per-tile operating state, and readiness inputs; cgx1_top_tb covers arbitrary eligible subsets and emergency masking. The previously reported hardwired P1/P2 count mismatch is not present in current RTL. Connecting the eligibility producer through global placement into per-CU dispatch, tile-state sequencing, and physical isolation or gating remain open.

Post-decode control supports a 57-bit aligned per-wave PC, live/active lane masks, branch joins, calls/returns with active-frame depth protection, structured loops with call-depth unwind, lane termination, and bounded-stack faults. The workgroup frontend integrates dispatch initialization, accepted-instruction PC advance, active vector/LSU masks, and barrier reconvergence through the residency authority's committed local-to-slot map. C++ and full local RTL gates passed on the current candidate. Opcode formats, fetch/decode, compiler lowering, full per-wave instruction issue, runtime dispatch, and physical evidence remain open.

One CU has an executable and RTL decoded-compute workgroup dispatcher with bounded per-context FIFO storage, weighted priority service with aging, tile-eligibility and queue-fault gating, retryable versus terminal admission results, and integration with the authoritative workgroup frontend. The dispatcher arbitrates workgroups; it does not own per-wave instruction issue or queue-context allocation. A bounded C++ command-packet reference now feeds it. RTL packet processing, the I/O-die global queue manager, public ABI freeze, graphics dispatch, multi-CU/tile placement, compiler/runtime submission and completion, calibrated performance, synthesis, and physical evidence remain open.
Architecture targets exist; the global LSU boundary remains abstract and there is no cache, translation, or physical memory backend.
Multi-CU placement, tile-to-fabric traffic, coherence, and contention are architecture targets without an integrated executable model or RTL path.
Graphics, texture, and compression contracts exist, but no shared-machine graphics execution path is implemented.

A bounded C++ reference parses a provisional little-endian workgroup-dispatch packet, feeds the existing CU dispatch scheduler, and reports completion after admission or quiescent retirement. RTL now locally integrates parameterized per-context rings, round-robin complete-frame feeding, the existing parser, and one CU dispatcher, preserving packet identity through CU admission; this integration is not wired into cgx1_top. Ingress recovery drops unread bytes and clears parser fault state but does not cancel complete parser-output or dispatcher-owned descriptors. RTL queue unregister/reuse, full reset/cancellation across lifecycle owners, global queue arbitration, and retirement-based command completion remain open. Parser errors remain separate from final workgroup completion. The packet format is not a frozen public ABI. Graphics packets, compiler lowering, kernel/object loading, grid/argument ABI, host runtime APIs, multi-CU placement, SRAM implementation, and all physical evidence remain open.
Some logical RTL exists, but no synthesis, timing, area, power, floorplan, placement, routing, or silicon evidence is present.
